conflict_topics: seat reservation/ownership at the two-seat table
competition for a single newly opened seat
evaluation.final_reason: The initial dispute over the occupied two-seat table remained unresolved until A proposed moving to an open seat; that created a separate, unresolved contest between A and D for one newly available seat. By the transcript end both A and D claim the single open seat and no settlement or transfer of the seat is completed.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A claims the seat (left tissue packet), Agent B refuses to move because bowl is open, and Agent D supports finding another seat; positions are directly incompatible about who should occupy the disputed seat.
Agents A and B repeat their opposing claims (A insists the seat was reserved, B insists they cannot move due to open bowl); no substantive concession or arrangement is reached.

Positions remain the same: A continues to demand the seat to eat during a short break, B continues to refuse due to risk of spilling; C calls for sharing/keeping aisle clear but offers no binding solution.
A declares intent to take a newly opened seat elsewhere; D immediately claims that same single available seat as well, creating a new direct contest between A and D over one seat.

A asserts need to sit and B permits A to take the seat, while D simultaneously asserts he will take the seat; both A and D claim the same seat and no agreement is reached (and a third diner is approaching).
